# From subspace arrangements generated by small intersections to ternary codes

Work over F₃. A subspace arrangement is an ordered indexed list S₁,…,Sₘ of subspaces of an explicit ambient space V, with a color on each index and one marked union of colors. A comparison asks for a color-preserving bijection σ of the indices and one ambient linear isomorphism taking Sᵢ to S′_{σ(i)}. The permutation on the marked indices must be even in their input orders. Write U for this problem and C for the analogous even coordinate-permutation equivalence problem for explicit ternary linear codes. This proof is informal. All reductions are deterministic polynomial-time many-one reductions.

## The sufficient condition

Fix a positive integer k and a constant c>0. Let L be the length of the whole comparison and set w=⌊c log₃(max(2,L))⌋. Regard one endpoint as the labeled representation of the star quiver, with one incoming inclusion Sᵢ→V at vertex i. Decompose this representation into indecomposable direct summands, retaining each copy. Write V_B for the central space of a summand, and S_{B,i} for its subspace at label i. For a summand B compute two sets:

* P_B contains every nonzero vector in each intersection of at most k of the S_{B,i} which has dimension at most w.
* D_B contains every nonzero covector in each intersection of at most k of the annihilators S_{B,i}° in V_B* which has dimension at most w.

In both cases take the union without duplicates and use only nonempty index collections. Test whether, for every B and i, at least one of these equations holds:

    S_{B,i} = span(P_B ∩ S_{B,i}),
    S_{B,i}° = span(D_B ∩ S_{B,i}°).

The span of an empty set is zero. This condition is preserved under isomorphism, including a simultaneous permutation of the labels. On the recognizable family satisfying it, one can reduce U to one instance of C while preserving all feasible label permutations. Thus an additional independent ordinary TI comparison can be carried unchanged, giving the corresponding reverse on that family in the ladder. The threshold can also be defined using a common polynomially bounded parameter indexed by the pair. Membership and the reduction run in polynomial time for fixed k and c.

The decomposition algorithm used here is Chistov, Ivanyos and Karpinski, Theorem 5, which runs deterministically in time polynomial in the input size and the field characteristic. The algebra in this case is the path algebra of the star with identity vertex idempotents, arrow maps and no length-two paths. Its structure constants and module action have polynomial size. Each summand's inclusion maps stay injective. The Krull–Schmidt theorem gives invariance of the multiset of summands with multiplicity when labels are held fixed. Relabeling the leaves permutes the vertex idempotents and arrows, so the same uniqueness applies after any proposed label permutation. This permits arbitrary independently computed indecomposable decompositions of the two inputs. [Chistov, Ivanyos and Karpinski](https://theory.cs.uni-bonn.de/marek/publications/85169-cs.pdf)

## Extending a partial vector and covector transport

Let P⊆V and D⊆V* be the linear spans of two collections of vectors and covectors. Let P′⊆V′ and D′⊆V′* have the same respective dimensions. Suppose dim V=dim V′ and isomorphisms g₀:P→P′ and h₀:D→D′ obey

    h₀(f)(g₀(v)) = f(v) for every v∈P and f∈D.

Then there is a linear isomorphism g:V→V′ with g|P=g₀ and (g⁻¹)*|D=h₀. To see this, put N=ann(D)⊆V and N′=ann(D′)⊆V′. The evaluation maps identify V/N with D* and V′/N′ with D′*. Their induced quotient map is forced to be (h₀⁻¹)*. The stated pairing equation guarantees that g₀ maps P∩N onto P′∩N′ and induces this required quotient map on the image of P. Choose a basis of P∩N and extend it to a basis of N, matching g₀ on the initial vectors. Then adjoin vectors of P whose image gives a basis of (P+N)/N, matched by g₀. Finally lift a basis of the remaining quotient coordinates and match them by the forced quotient map. The resulting isomorphism has both required restrictions. The proof allows either span to be zero.

## Color the parity coordinates and the common label constraints

Use the span of the following column vectors as the ambient space for a generator matrix. All indicated spaces are independent direct summands. Give the global label space the basis e_i, and the global summand-index space the basis f_B. Include one primal span span(P_B) and one dual span span(D_B) for each B.

Include these columns, with distinct palettes for the different types of records.

1. Include e_i with the old label color and mark. Keep those marked columns in their original relative order. Include f_B with a color recording dim V_B.
2. Include each nonzero p∈P_B as a primal vector column, and each nonzero d∈D_B as a dual vector column. Link them to their summand by the columns f_B+p and f_B+d in separate palettes.
3. For each B,i include f_B+e_i with a color indicating whether this entry uses the primal or dual equation. Prefer primal whenever it holds. For a primal entry add all f_B+e_i+p for p∈P_B∩S_{B,i}. For a dual entry add all f_B+e_i+d for d∈D_B∩S_{B,i}°. The primal and dual membership columns have separate colors, disjoint from all other palettes.
4. For each B and p∈P_B,d∈D_B include the column p+d, in an evaluation palette colored by the value d(p)∈F₃. These use the actual vector and covector representatives, so a color directly records the value.

The row span of the resulting full-row-rank generator matrix is the output code. It has full row rank because the individual tag columns and vector and covector banks span their declared spaces. A color-preserving permutation of its columns yields the same row-space code as the target exactly when a linear isomorphism on these ambient generator coordinates takes each source column to its target column. This is the usual generator-matrix description of permutation code equivalence.

## Correctness and size

From a code transporter the individually colored palettes give a common label permutation σ on the e_i and a dimension-preserving permutation τ on the f_B. The primal and dual palettes force their full spans to be preserved as separate direct sums. The link columns from item 2 then force every vector and covector to move to the summand τ(B). In particular they restrict the code's linear map to linear isomorphisms between the primal spans and between the dual spans within each matched summand. Item 4 forces preservation of each evaluation exactly, since the two components of a sum determine its unique primal and dual entries. Evaluation is bilinear and the banks span, so the equality extends to the two spans. The extension lemma gives one ambient map on V_B carrying the two kinds of selected entries to their corresponding entries, by item 3 and the generation conditions. The direct sum of these maps takes all the original subspaces under the one permutation σ. The parity requirement uses only the e_i that carried the original mark, so its sign is exact.

Conversely a valid arrangement transporter inducing σ identifies the multisets of independently chosen indecomposables after relabeling. Choose an isomorphism of summands for this matching. Each such local map preserves the membership choices, the primal and dual banks as vector sets, and the evaluations, because dimensions, intersections, spans and annihilators commute with transport. The local maps and the common tag permutation therefore give a column isomorphism as specified. This preserves σ and its marked parity. In either direction the construction works for duplicated and empty subspaces.

For each summand there are at most Σ_{j=1}^{k} binom(m,j) intersection candidates on either side. A retained space has at most 3^w vectors. All spans, annihilators, intersections and membership tests use ordinary Gaussian elimination. The number of summands is bounded by the ambient dimension, since the inclusions imply every nonzero summand has a nonzero central space. The evaluation table uses at most the product of the two bank sizes for each summand. The resulting coefficient arrays, tags and colors all have polynomial length. An eligible source and an ineligible target have no transporter by invariance. This is handled by a fixed negative comparison. For the restricted comparison problem, any noneligible endpoint is likewise a rejection.

## Families exceeding direct point enumeration

Taking k=1 includes arbitrary mixtures of subspaces with logarithmic dimension and subspaces with logarithmic codimension. The algorithm also covers simultaneous direct sums of such local arrangements, even with very large raw subspace dimensions and codimensions. It recovers the decomposition itself rather than requiring it as input.

Small intersections further cover arrangements with large indecomposable blocks and no small raw subspace at all. For example take V=F₃^{2r} with r≥2. For every coordinate vector e_i include two coordinate r-spaces intersecting in exactly the line span(e_i). Their remaining r−1 coordinate vectors can be chosen from disjoint sets. For every i<2r include two r-spaces generated by e_i+e_{i+1} and disjoint sets of r−1 remaining coordinate basis vectors outside its two-coordinate support. The latter pair intersects exactly in span(e_i+e_{i+1}). Each subspace is recovered by its bank of vectors in the pairwise intersections. Every raw subspace has both dimension and codimension r, and the list has only linear length in r. Any endomorphism preserving the labeled arrangement preserves the coordinate lines and the adjacent-sum lines. The former make the map diagonal and the latter make all its diagonal entries equal. Therefore the endomorphism algebra is the scalar field and the representation is indecomposable. This shows that the criterion can apply even when each local subspace and the sole indecomposable summand are too large for direct enumeration.

The reduction gives a sufficient condition for eliminating arbitrary block-basis changes in the subspace-to-code comparison. It does not settle the unrestricted reverse for arrangements outside the generation condition.
